list_datasets.title: List approved datasets
list_datasets.description: List every dataset this application's server token is approved for, with each dataset's id, `datasetCode` (the code every MLS tool takes as dataset), name and description. Start here to find which dataset codes you can query. For the RESO DataSystem view with resource listings per dataset use list_data_systems.

output.description: Bridge envelope with `total` and `bundle`, the array of datasets (id, datasetCode, name, description).

list_data_systems.title: List RESO data systems
list_data_systems.description: Return the RESO Web API DataSystem resource: one entry per dataset the token can reach, with its ID (dataset code), Name, ServiceURI, transport and Data Dictionary versions and the Resources (Property, Member, Office, OpenHouse, ...) it exposes. Use list_datasets for the simpler native list.

output.description: OData collection; `value` lists the data systems and their resources.

get_reso_metadata.title: Get dataset metadata (RESO)
get_reso_metadata.description: Fetch the RESO Web API $metadata document for a dataset: every entity type, field, data type and lookup value the data provider has made available to this application. Returned as OData EDMX XML, not JSON. Not available for virtual datasets. Use query_lookups for lookup values as JSON.

dataset.description: Dataset code to query, e.g. `test` or an MLS code such as `recolorado` (list_datasets returns the codes this application is approved for). A virtual dataset code also works for on-demand queries.

output.description: The EDMX XML metadata document as text.

query_properties.title: Query properties (RESO)
query_properties.description: Query Property (listing) records normalized to the RESO Data Dictionary, including the Media array of photos on each record in a dataset with the RESO Web API (OData), filtering with $filter and shaping with $select/$orderby/$expand. Returns up to 200 per page; use skip or the next cursor to page, and replicate_properties for more than 10,000 records. Fetch one by key with get_property_reso.

dataset.description: Dataset code to query, e.g. `test` or an MLS code such as `recolorado` (list_datasets returns the codes this application is approved for). A virtual dataset code also works for on-demand queries.

filter.description: OData $filter expression using RESO Data Dictionary field names. Operators: eq, ne, gt, lt, ge, le, and, or, not; functions: any/all on arrays, geo.distance, geo.intersects, tolower, startswith, endswith, contains, date, time, year, month, day, hour, now(). Strings in single quotes, e.g. `StandardStatus eq 'Active' and ListPrice gt 100000` or `geo.distance(Coordinates, POINT(-118.62 34.22)) lt 0.5`. Queries are case-sensitive; wrap a field in tolower() to work around it.

select.description: Only return these fields (sent comma-separated). When expanding, include the expanded navigation field too (e.g. ListOffice).

unselect.description: Fields to leave out of the response (sent comma-separated), e.g. ["Media"] to drop the photo list.

top.description: Records to return. Provider default 10, maximum 200.

skip.description: Skip this many records; paginate by incrementing skip by top (up to 10,000 records; beyond that use the replication tool).

orderby.description: Sort expression: a field name plus `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `ListPrice desc` or `ModificationTimestamp asc`.

expand.description: Related entities to include inline (sent comma-separated): ListAgent, CoListAgent, BuyerAgent, CoBuyerAgent, ListOffice, CoListOffice. Not every query option applies to expanded data.

next.description: The `$next` cursor taken from the previous response's `@odata.nextLink`, to fetch the following page.

output.description: An OData collection: `value` holds the Property records; `@odata.nextLink` is the URL of the next page (its `$next` cursor can be passed back as next) and `@odata.count` the total when returned.

list_listings.title: List listings
list_listings.description: List MLS listings (RESO-normalized Property records with Media) from a dataset with the Bridge Web API's simple native syntax: limit/offset paging (max 200), sortBy/order, field selection, and geographic search by near+radius, box, polygon or geohash. For field-level filters such as ListPrice.gt=500000 use search_mls_native; for OData $filter queries use the RESO tools (query_properties).

dataset.description: Dataset code to query, e.g. `test` or an MLS code such as `recolorado` (list_datasets returns the codes this application is approved for). A virtual dataset code also works for on-demand queries.

offset.description: Skip this number of results (provider default 0). Paginate by incrementing offset by limit; always sort when paginating, since order is not otherwise guaranteed.

limit.description: Size of the result set. Provider default 10, maximum 200.

sort_by.description: Response field to sort by, e.g. `ListPrice` or `BridgeModificationTimestamp`.

fields.description: Only return these response fields (sent comma-separated), e.g. ["ListingKey", "ListPrice"]. Smaller payloads are faster.

near.description: Centre point as `{lng},{lat}` (decimal degrees, longitude first) or a place name, e.g. `-122.395743,37.793662` or `San Diego`.

radius.description: Search radius around `near`; suffix `mi` (miles, default) or `km`, or a bare number of degrees, e.g. `5mi`. Provider default 10.

poly.description: Polygon of at least 3 coordinate pairs as `{lng1},{lat1},{lng2},{lat2},...,{lngN},{latN}`.

geohash.description: Alphanumeric geohash cell to search within, e.g. `ezs42`.

output.description: The Bridge envelope: `success`, `status`, `total` (count of matching records) and `bundle`, the array of listings.

get_listing.title: Get one listing
get_listing.description: Fetch a single listing by its key with the Bridge Web API. Returns the record object (unwrapped from `bundle`), optionally trimmed to the listed fields. Use list_listings to search instead.

dataset.description: Dataset code to query, e.g. `test` or an MLS code such as `recolorado` (list_datasets returns the codes this application is approved for). A virtual dataset code also works for on-demand queries.

listing_id.description: The listing's key (ListingKey) as returned by list_listings.

fields.description: Only return these response fields (sent comma-separated), e.g. ["ListingKey", "ListPrice"]. Smaller payloads are faster.

output.description: The listing record, unwrapped from the Bridge envelope's `bundle`.

query_agent_reviews.title: Query Zillow agent reviews
query_agent_reviews.description: Query Zillow Agent Reviews: each review has Rating, Description, ReviewDate, ReviewerScreenName, ServiceProviderDesc, ServiceYear, location names, RevieweeKey and TeamLeadAccountId. Holds the 10 most recent reviews per reviewee; filter e.g. `RevieweeKey eq 'f0406f76c3c46b10494c29dc'`. To find an agent first, use query_agent_reviewees.

filter.description: OData $filter expression using RESO Data Dictionary field names. Operators: eq, ne, gt, lt, ge, le, and, or, not; functions: any/all on arrays, geo.distance, geo.intersects, tolower, startswith, endswith, contains, date, time, year, month, day, hour, now(). Strings in single quotes, e.g. `StandardStatus eq 'Active' and ListPrice gt 100000` or `geo.distance(Coordinates, POINT(-118.62 34.22)) lt 0.5`. Queries are case-sensitive; wrap a field in tolower() to work around it.

select.description: Only return these fields (sent comma-separated). When expanding, include the expanded navigation field too (e.g. ListOffice).

unselect.description: Fields to leave out of the response (sent comma-separated), e.g. ["Media"] to drop the photo list.

top.description: Records to return. Provider default 10, maximum 200.

skip.description: Skip this many records; paginate by incrementing skip by top (up to 10,000 records; beyond that use the replication tool).

orderby.description: Sort expression: a field name plus `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `ListPrice desc` or `ModificationTimestamp asc`.

next.description: The `$next` cursor taken from the previous response's `@odata.nextLink`, to fetch the following page.

output.description: An OData collection: `value` holds the reviews; `@odata.nextLink` is the URL of the next page (its `$next` cursor can be passed back as next) and `@odata.count` the total when returned.
